caption: The drawing features a single, old-fashioned lantern or lamp as its central object, depicted with realistic detail. The lantern is composed of a rounded, transparent glass body through which reflections and highlights are visible, suggesting the presence of a light source inside. The base, top, and handle of the lantern are made of a brownish metal, with the top section being conical and having a circular loop for carrying or hanging. Small holes are visible in the upper part for ventilation. The color palette consists mostly of shades of brown for the metal parts and neutral tones with white highlights for the glass. The lantern is centered within a rectangular frame drawn in thin lines, set against a plain, light background with no additional objects or details. The name "Manuel G. Runyan" is written in small letters near the bottom right corner of the drawing.
title: Street Hanging Lamp
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
